cues.title: Enter at speaking volume
cues.text: Start with an easy, clean onset. Keep the phrase intimate and forward instead of adding breath or weight to announce the first note.

cues.title: Keep vowels tall
cues.text: Let consonants pass quickly and give the vowels the time. Avoid spreading the mouth as the melody rises.

cues.title: Connect the thought
cues.text: Sing the line as one speech gesture. Reduce final consonants enough that they do not interrupt the legato.

cues.title: Lift without pushing
cues.text: Increase intention before volume. Keep the resonance forward and allow the pitch lift to happen on steady air.

cues.title: Hold the pocket
cues.text: Stay slightly behind the beat while keeping the vowels connected. Do not rush the short notes between sustained tones.

cues.title: Let intensity grow gradually
cues.text: Build through resonance, not throat pressure. Keep the jaw released so the longer tones can taper naturally.

cues.title: Reset to conversational
cues.text: Return to a smaller sound after the chorus. Clear diction comes from precise tongue movement, not heavier consonants.

cues.title: Prepare the upper notes early
cues.text: Narrow the vowel before the pitch rises. Keep the breath pressure stable and let the placement move higher.

cues.title: Shape the dynamic contrast
cues.text: Begin close and understated, then grow only on the important words. Preserve the relaxed R&B phrasing throughout.

cues.title: Map the pitch turns
cues.text: Practice the contour slowly first. Keep each fast change connected to one breath rather than attacking every note separately.

cues.title: Finish with release
cues.text: Keep the final phrases energized while allowing their ends to fade. Do not hold extra air pressure after the pitch resolves.
